key_insight: The paper formalizes user–decoder co-adaptation in closed‑loop neural interfaces as an interaction governed by control and game theory, and uses that formalism to predict and shape learning dynamics so systems become more usable and personalized.
problem_solved: Unpredictable, user‑specific co‑adaptation in closed‑loop brain–machine interfaces makes it hard to design decoders and adaptation rules that reliably improve performance and user experience.
method: Model the user and decoder as coupled adaptive agents (a game/control system) to capture bidirectional learning dynamics.
Analyze stability and equilibria using control‑ and game‑theoretic tools to predict long‑term interaction outcomes.
Derive design principles and adaptation policies for decoders that steer the joint system toward desirable, personalized behaviors.
impact: Provides a principled toolkit for designing and tuning adaptive neural interfaces, improving reliability, personalization, and long‑term performance; concepts transfer to other closed‑loop ML systems where humans and models co‑adapt.
visual_elements: Closed‑loop schematic: user ↔ neural decoder ↔ device loop with arrows showing bidirectional adaptation
Phase/dynamics plot: trajectories showing different stable equilibria under varying decoder policies
Before/after performance chart: learning curves comparing naive vs. theory‑guided adaptation
Design rule infographic: icons linking control/game‑theory analysis → decoder policy → improved usability
paper_title: Computational framework to predict and shape human–machine interactions in closed-loop, co-adaptive neural interfaces
paper_authors: Maneeshika M. Madduri, Momona Yamagami, Si Jia Li, Sasha Burckhardt, Samuel A. Burden
